newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER ENDS UP ON RINGGIT ADJUSTMENT.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER ENDS UP ON RINGGIT ADJUSTMENT.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on Wednesday on a technical rise linked to the weakness of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
"It's basically a price adjustment to reflect the current level of the currency," said a trader. "You won't find any fundamentals behind it."
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7860 to a dollar in Kuala Lumpur, after opening at 2.7785.
Dealers said they had not heard of any business for the day, and that trading volumes were thin at the best.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for September buyer at 249.50 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Tuesday.
The SMR20 for September buyer was half cent higher at 248.50 cents a kg.
For Aug/Sept, trading houses were offering the SMR 20 at 248 cents a kg, while the SMR CV at 289 cents, SMR L at 270, SMR 5 at 260, SMR 10 at 250 and drum latex at 192.
